A half-day course that alternates **short lectures**, **live demonstrations**, and **hands-on exercises**. Timings are targets — we'll flex to keep the hands-on blocks intact.

::: {.callout-tip}
## How we'll navigate
We'll run the course from this website — I'll share my screen and click through pages so you can copy-paste along. For the lecture blocks I'll switch to [slides](slides/foundations.qmd); when we build, we come back here.
:::

## Run of show

### [8:35]{.chip} Welcome & the "watch this" demo · 15 min
Before any theory, I'll open Claude Code, **dictate a task out loud**, and set it working on a real project in the background — then we start the lecture while it runs. The point is to *feel* what "directing an agent" means before we define it.

### [8:50]{.chip} Module 1 · Foundations · 30 min
[Foundations →](foundations.qmd) · [slides](slides/foundations.qmd)

What agentic coding actually is: an LLM that can use **tools** (read files, run code, edit, search) in a loop. The landscape of tools. The vocabulary you'll hear. Where this helps research — and where to be careful.

### [9:20]{.chip} Module 2 · Prompting & directing · 35 min
[Prompting →](prompting.qmd) · [slides](slides/prompting.qmd) · **Exercise 1**

How to prompt effectively, scope context, plan before acting, and review output. Meet `CLAUDE.md`. Then you run your **[first agent session](exercises/ex1-first-session.qmd)**.

### [9:55]{.chip} Break · 10 min

### [10:05]{.chip} Module 3 · Git & GitHub · 45 min
[Git & GitHub →](git-github.qmd) · [slides](slides/git-github.qmd) · **Exercises 2 & 3**

Version control reframed as the **operating system for safe agent collaboration**: commits, branches, pull requests, and merging only what you approve. You'll direct an agent through a full **[branch → PR → review → merge](exercises/ex2-git-with-agent.qmd)** loop, then **[write a `CLAUDE.md`](exercises/ex3-claude-md.qmd)** for a project.

### [10:50]{.chip} Module 4 · Skills & workflows · 30 min
[Skills & workflows →](skills.qmd) · [slides](slides/skills.qmd) · **Exercise 4**

Customizing an agent for *your* recurring tasks. What a skill is, when to write one, and the anatomy of a good one. You'll **[write your first skill](exercises/ex4-first-skill.qmd)** — the course's core deliverable.

### [11:20]{.chip} Module 5 · Build session · 35 min
[Build session →](build-session.qmd) · **Exercise 5**

The rest is yours. Bring a research task and **[prototype a workflow](exercises/ex5-your-workflow.qmd)** for it, with me and others available to help.

### [11:55]{.chip} Wrap-up · 5 min
Share what you built, where to go deeper, and how to keep developing your workflow after today.

## What to have open

- This website.
- A terminal in a folder where you can make a scratch project.
- Claude Code (`claude`), signed in.
- Your GitHub account in a browser tab.
- A research task in mind for the build session.
